svg.title: Japan at a glance — single-page static SVG infographic
svg.desc: A modern editorial infographic on Japan with soft gradient background, waves, cards, a stylized map with cities, explanatory text, a GDP bar chart (2015–2024), a population composition donut chart, travel highlights, and source notes. No JavaScript or external images.

g.text: Major cities plotted approximately. Stylized silhouette for context.

text.tspan: An island nation in East Asia, Japan spans a long arc across the Pacific,
from Hokkaidō in the north to Kyūshū and Okinawa in the south. It blends
deep cultural traditions with cutting-edge technology and design.

g.text: Population: ~125 million; Life expectancy among the world’s highest
World leader in autos, electronics, robotics, materials, and precision tools
Transport: renowned Shinkansen high‑speed rail, dense metro networks

text.tspan: 3rd largest economy by nominal GDP; strong export base;
structural shifts and currency effects shape recent trends.

g.text: Japan’s archipelago concentrates people and industry along coastal plains while mountains and forests define much of the interior. A mature, innovation‑driven economy coexists with craft traditions, seasonal cuisine, and a distinctive design language that informs everything from packaging to architecture and transit.

text.tspan: • Key sectors: automotive, electronics, machinery, chemicals,
• Major trading partners: China, U.S., EU, South Korea, ASEAN.
research, global supply chains, brand trust.
• Challenges: demographics, productivity, energy mix, yen cycles.

g.text: Nominal values reflect current U.S. dollars. Currency movements and domestic price levels
affect cross‑country comparisons year to year.
Source: World Bank, IMF (nominal USD). Bars scaled to 0–5.5T.
Note: shares rounded; small communities are growing via study and work programs.
Skytree views, Shibuya/Sensō‑ji, contemporary art/design, food scenes.
Temples and gardens (Kiyomizu‑dera, Fushimi Inari), tea, crafts, machiya lanes.
Dōtonbori neon, castle park, street food (takoyaki, okonomiyaki).
Peace Memorial, Itsukushima Shrine’s torii, oysters and sea views.
Iconic vistas, lakeside trails, onsen, ropeways and art museums.
Sapporo culture, national parks, powder snow, summer wildflowers.

Data notes: GDP values (nominal US$ trillions, 2015–2024) from World Bank and IMF releases; population composition shares from Japan’s Statistics Bureau and MOJ (approximate, rounded). This graphic is illustrative; map placement of cities is approximate for orientation.
